claims.text: A 1-year-old female Dalmatian presented with a 6-cm subcutaneous nodule near the right ischial tuberosity, with irregular borders, overlying erythema and mild mobility. The nodule was not painful on palpation, was not discomforting and did not interfere with walking, defecating or lying down. The differential diagnoses included a perianal hernia, anal sac fistula or abscess, and hygroma.

claims.text: Fine needle aspiration cytology was performed to determine whether the nodule was inflammatory or neoplastic, using a 5-ml syringe and a 21-gauge needle. Serosanguineous, viscous fluid (5 ml) was aspirated, smeared, air-dried, stained with a rapid hemocolorant and evaluated by a veterinary clinical pathologist. Microscopy showed spindle cells, round cells consistent with histiocytes and a mucoid matrix with macrophages, and cytological findings did not indicate neoplastic, inflammatory or degenerative changes. A presumptive diagnosis of a ganglion cyst was made.
